conf.description: Palo Alto NGFW Traffic log (syslog-csv, PAN-OS 10.2/11.1), direct route: positional CSV parse of the 20 mapped columns to ECS + panw.panos.session_id, action-driven event.outcome, drop _raw per recommendations.direct.cribl (highest-volume/lowest-forensic-value of the four PAN-OS datasets)

conf.comment: Palo Alto NGFW Traffic log, syslog-csv, direct route. Positional parse via comma-count regex (same idiom as the live palo_alto_traffic reference pipeline: skip-N-then-capture). Only the 20 work-order field rows are captured; device_name/observer.name is NOT mapped here - its CSV column position beyond ~35 could not be cross-validated against the reference pipeline's confirmed offsets (which only reach field 34/Bytes Received) and is left as a documented gap rather than guessed. event.outcome is derived from action before the rename so it reads the flat vendor field, not the post-rename nested event.action.

functions.description: Pipeline purpose and the device_name gap
Message body: a Cribl Syslog Source leaves the full line, header included, in _raw and the body in message; anything else carries the body in _raw.
Positional capture of time_generated (field 7) and the 19 traffic-log columns through Packets (field 35), skipping the intervening PAN-OS CSV columns by count
Derive event.outcome from the vendor action value BEFORE rename (reads the flat field; a post-rename event.action would be a nested path and read as undefined)
Batch rename of all 19 mapped/custom columns to their ECS/custom targets
Set _time from the CSV Generated Time column (field 7); Elastic destination maps _time onward to @timestamp
Tag event.dataset; drop the now-redundant time_generated and drop _raw per recommendations.direct.cribl's explicit instruction for this dataset (highest volume, lowest forensic value of the four)
Re-nest flat dotted keys (data-maps canonical step)
